posts.title: Props that can take the load are still unsafe if the slab they sit on cannot
posts.excerpt: CROSS-UK Report 1539 (14 May 2026): temporary props for replacing a defective RC column in a multi-storey block were already installed. The props could carry over 1,165 kN characteristic / about 1,590 kN design. Opening-up showed the existing beams and slabs would fail in bending and shear. The drawing was For Approval and pushed the existing-structure check onto the client. HSE 15 June 2026 Paxton House prosecution: temporary platforms with no design and no calculated safe load collapsed onto a drilling operative.
posts.linkedinReady:
A pair of heavy-duty props is not a temporary works scheme if nobody has checked the slab and beams they sit on.

CROSS-UK Report 1539 (14 May 2026) describes a defective RC column at the base of a multi-storey block of flats. Characteristic load over 1,165 kN. Design load about 1,590 kN. Props were already on site. The drawing was marked For Approval and carried a caveat that the client must confirm the existing structure could take the extra load. The props themselves could carry the force. Opening-up then showed the existing beams and slabs would fail in bending and shear under the redistributed load. The Reporter designed a more complex scheme and a written method. Without that work, a significant part of the building was at risk of collapse.

The Expert Panel called it a failure of the temporary works procedure: TWC and checker missing on a significant structure, and a brief that designed the kit in isolation from the load path to a foundation.

HSE June 2026 Paxton House prosecution is the same lesson from the other end. Temporary wooden platforms under core-drilled openings had no design and no calculated safe load. Debris accumulated. The platform collapsed onto Steve Zschoch. Neck and back fractures. Two contractors fined under CDM 2015.

For contractors: the brief must include the existing structure. Caveats on a For Approval drawing do not transfer the check. Register the scheme, name the TWC, get opening-up and a load-path check before anyone takes a column out.

body.p: CROSS-UK published Safety Report 1539 on 14 May 2026. A Reporter was asked to advise on temporary works to remove a defective reinforced concrete column at the base of a multi-storey block of flats and replace it with a new steel column. Estimated characteristic load on the column was over 1,165 kN and estimated design load approximately 1,590 kN. On arrival, heavy-duty props were already installed. The prop designer had left a drawing showing pairs of props under the beams and slab either side of the column. Status: For Approval. A note on the drawing said the client must be assured the scheme was safe and suitable and that, if the system created additional loads on an existing structure, the structure could safely support those loads. The props themselves could take the required forces. There was no evidence the existing structure had been checked. Opening-up to establish beam size, slab thickness and reinforcement showed the existing beams and slabs were not strong enough to transfer load from the props to the concrete column above and would fail in bending and shear. The Reporter designed a more complex temporary works system and a written method statement. The contractor could have removed the defective column without those additional works; the Reporter considered it likely that a significant part of the building would have collapsed.

The CROSS Expert Panel described the report as worrying and as a failure of the temporary works procedure that should have been in place, with a Temporary Works Coordinator and checking engineer appointed on what sounded like a significant structure. When temporary works support an existing structure, a viable load path must be understood and verified from the point of application through to a suitable foundation. Designing props in isolation creates unsafe assumptions if the surrounding structure has not been assessed. In this case the column above continues to load the system; beams that previously took one floor into the column now have to carry shear from more floors. The Panel pointed to similar CROSS material, including Report 1459 on inadequate propping of an existing timber beam. Competent engineers should recognise an incomplete brief and advise accordingly. Refurbishment increases the number of complex temporary conditions.

On 15 June 2026 the Health and Safety Executive published the outcome of a prosecution after a temporary platform collapse at Paxton House in the City of London on 23 February 2024. Principal contractor Roots Contractors Limited had instructed carpenters to build temporary wooden platforms under openings being cut through five concrete floors to form a service riser. The platforms were to collect 16 kg concrete cores and debris. Drilling operative Steve Zschoch, working for Diacutt Limited, was cutting on the third floor under one of the platforms when it collapsed with uncleared concrete. He sustained fractures to his neck and back and a bleed on the brain. HSE found no design for the platforms and no calculation of a safe load. An inspection form had been completed by someone who was not a competent Temporary Works Coordinator. Roots Contractors Limited pleaded guilty to CDM 2015 Regulation 16(2) and was fined 19333 pounds plus 5548 pounds costs at Westminster Magistrates Court on 11 June 2026. Diacutt Limited pleaded guilty to CDM 2015 Regulation 15(2) and was fined 13000 pounds plus 5548 pounds costs.

Column replacement, riser cutting, crash decks and propping of existing floors are temporary works. The kit capacity is only one line in the check. The existing slab, beam, wall and foundation that receive the load are part of the same scheme. BS 5975-1:2024 is the management procedure that puts the item on the register, names a Temporary Works Coordinator and Temporary Works Supervisor, requires a design brief that includes the existing structure, and requires an independent check and permit before load is taken or a column is removed. A For Approval drawing that caves the existing-structure check back to the client is not a completed design. A wooden platform built by carpenters to catch cores is not automatically low risk because it is timber. Occupied multi-storey buildings, high column loads and debris accumulation all escalate.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Register column replacement, floor openings, crash decks and propping of existing structure as temporary works before the first prop is stood or the first core is cut.

Issue a design brief that requires the existing load path to be verified: beam and slab size, reinforcement, condition, foundations, and the number of storeys that will now travel through those members.
Do not accept a For Approval drawing whose only existing-structure clause is a client caveat. That is a gap, not a check.
Opening-up before load: dimensions, cover, bar size and spacing, defects. If the structure cannot take the prop loads, redesign.
Provisional design and check category only to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

Hold points: brief accepted, existing structure checked, scheme checked, inspection before load, permit-to-load, exclusion of people under loaded platforms, debris clearance to a stated limit, permit before column removal.
Name a competent person for inspection. Completing a form is not the same as being the TWC.
Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Not a design, not a check and not a permit. Subject to project-specific verification of loads, existing-structure capacity, sequence and responsible persons, and to acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. Facts are taken from CROSS-UK Report 1539 published 14 May 2026 and the HSE Media Centre release of 15 June 2026; confirm against those pages before relying on them. Exact clause references in CDM 2015 and BS 5975-1:2024 are to be confirmed against the project licensed copy. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.
